title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
synopsis: Macondo. A town founded between a river and a swamp. Your family is the Buendía family. The world will come for you, slowly, in seven generations.

nodes.text: José Arcadio Buendía draws Macondo on a map.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Path.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Practical.

nodes.text: Melquíades brings ice. Magnets. Flying carpets.

choices.consequence: “Buy them all” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Wonder.
You commit to “Save your money.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Mauricio Babilonia, mechanic, follows your aunt.

nodes.text: The town is, at last, a place that has been.

Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: The town is taken. The book ends. Generations after, in other cities, the book is read by people who do not know they are reading their own future.
A scholar in a quiet library, decades later, decodes the parchments fully. She publishes. The world reads. Macondo, against its own ending, persists.
Far from Macondo, descendants you didn't know about live ordinary lives. They name children, by chance, after you. They do not know why these names felt familiar.
